4.reviewNote: The layout behaves as (B) intends: /_t3flare/mcpx is the admin application's (302 to its Access login; with the service token the Worker's 404), /_t3flare/mcp/anything is the endpoint's (401 Bearer realm=OAuth with resource_metadata; admitted, 404). The script's check expected no WWW-Authenticate at all on the admin application's path, as m5a-stage-run.md item 4 implies; Access sends `Cloudflare-Access resource_metadata=…` with its 302 login on a non-OAuth application too (prod's /_t3flare/harness does, item 4c). The two applications are told apart by 302 login (scheme Cloudflare-Access) versus 401 (scheme Bearer realm=OAuth).

4c.reviewNote: Baseline recorded. Expectation partly wrong in m5a-stage-run.md item 4c and the report's deviation 27: /_t3flare/mcp on prod does get the admin application's Access login (302, same kid as /_t3flare/harness), but it does carry a `WWW-Authenticate: Cloudflare-Access resource_metadata=".../_t3flare/mcp"` header, as every path of that application does (/_t3flare/harness too). Access adds it to non-OAuth applications; it is not SettingsAccess. The discriminator after the first prod deploy with SettingsAccess is 401 with `Bearer realm="OAuth"` (the endpoint's) instead of 302 (the admin application's).
